scenarioStory.history: Bystanders report the patient's sedan drifted off the road at low speed and struck a mailbox post. On EMS arrival he is confused, diaphoretic, and repeating himself, with a small laceration to his forehead consistent with striking the steering wheel. A neighbor reached the patient's wife by phone, who confirms he is an insulin-dependent diabetic and skipped lunch today.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old male restrained in the driver's seat of a low-speed crash vehicle. He is diaphoretic, confused, and repeating himself, with a small forehead laceration. Mechanism and presentation raise both a metabolic and a traumatic differential. → Primary survey done, BGL checked, dextrose given: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey with spinal motion restriction, applies high-flow oxygen as a precaution for the head injury, checks blood glucose (32 mg/dL), and administers IV dextrose. Mental status begins improving but the crew continues treating this as a combined metabolic-and-trauma patient rather than assuming resolution. → Mental status normalizes, neuro monitoring continued: The patient's mental status returns to baseline after dextrose correction. The crew transports for head injury evaluation despite the resolved hypoglycemia, since the crash mechanism and forehead laceration still warrant a trauma workup.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old male restrained in the driver's seat of a low-speed crash vehicle. He is diaphoretic, confused, and repeating himself, with a small forehead laceration. Mechanism and presentation raise both a metabolic and a traumatic differential.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey with spinal precautions before treating suspected hypoglycemia
Apply high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather as a precaution for the head injury
Check point-of-care blood glucose given diaphoresis and confusion after the crash
Dextrose 10% IV in incremental doses (up to 250 mL / 25 g total) until mental status improves
Monitor blood pressure closely; target SBP ≥110 mmHg given the head injury

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey done, BGL checked, dextrose given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey with spinal motion restriction, applies high-flow oxygen as a precaution for the head injury, checks blood glucose (32 mg/dL), and administers IV dextrose. Mental status begins improving but the crew continues treating this as a combined metabolic-and-trauma patient rather than assuming resolution.
relatedChecklist: Continue serial neuro reassessment en route despite resolved hypoglycemia
Transport to an appropriate facility per field triage guideline given the head injury mechanism

scenarioEvents.name: Mental status normalizes, neuro monitoring continued
scenarioEvents.description: The patient's mental status returns to baseline after dextrose correction. The crew transports for head injury evaluation despite the resolved hypoglycemia, since the crash mechanism and forehead laceration still warrant a trauma workup.

scenarioEvents.name: AMS blamed on trauma alone, BGL not rechecked
scenarioEvents.description: The crew treats the confusion as purely trauma-related and does not recheck blood glucose. The hypoglycemia recurs and worsens, mimicking an expanding intracranial injury and delaying the correct treatment.
relatedChecklist: Recheck blood glucose given persistent AMS; treat recurrent hypoglycemia rather than assuming isolated TBI deterioration
